original.text: ācāryeṣvavamānena sugatājñāvilaṅghane | heyāt gotraguṇāsthāne mahāmaitrovivarjane || bodhicittaparityāge yānacitayanindane | guhyākhyāne jane pakṣe jinātaskandhadūṣaṇe ||
original.edition: Advayavajrasaṃgraha ed. H. P. Shastri (GOS 40, 1927), Muktabodha e-text M00510 (IAST by the unit; e-text misprints kept)
original.licence: Muktabodha e-text quoted for reference; terms of use as for the source file

paraphrase: The fourteen root downfalls of the mantra practitioner: despising the teachers; transgressing the Sugata's command; (anger toward vajra kin); abandoning love; abandoning bodhicitta; reviling the vehicles; revealing the secret to the unripe; abusing the aggregates (which are the Jinas); doubting the pure dharma; (misplaced) love for the wicked; superimposing (concepts) on non-dual dharmas; corrupting the minds of the faithful; not relying on the pledge substances when obtained; and disparaging women, who are of the nature of wisdom. Committing them, there are no attainments, Māra and a mass of suffering, and one experiences the intense pains of hell.
notes: The e-text is corrupt at downfalls 3 and 10; the items in parentheses follow the standard list.
